sources.title: Human History Map civilization index
sources.note: Exact Kuru identity, circa 500 to 400 BCE display interval, generated label and separately indexed neighboring records.

sources.title: Human History Map 700 BCE borders
sources.note: Decoded broad Vedic Indo-Aryans context layer and target absence before the exact Kuru interval.

sources.title: Human History Map 500 BCE borders
sources.note: Decoded exact Kuru polygon, topology, coordinate hash, point tests and simultaneous neighboring janapada layers.

sources.title: Human History Map 400 BCE borders
sources.note: Decoded target disappearance and generic Hindu Kingdoms replacement at the atlas endpoint.

sources.title: Human History Map 323 BCE borders
sources.note: Decoded later split between Magadha and a generic kingdoms-and-republics layer at tested Kuru-region points.

sources.title: Human History Map 300 BCE borders
sources.note: Decoded Maurya coverage at all tested Kuru-region points without treating it as an immediate 400 BCE successor.

sources.title: A. D. H. Bivar, The Indus Lands, Cambridge Ancient History
sources.note: Cambridge synthesis locating Kuru around Indraprastha on the upper Yamuna among northern India's local kingdoms and republics.

sources.title: Michael Witzel, Moving Targets?
sources.note: Peer-reviewed chronological warning that Late Vedic and earliest Buddhist texts belong to distinct historical layers.

sources.title: Michael Witzel, Early Sanskritization and Development of the Kuru State
sources.note: Peer-reviewed reconstruction of early Kuru political formation, ritual synthesis, constrained kingship and Parikshit praise.

sources.title: Geoffrey Samuel, Two worlds and their interactions
sources.note: Cambridge account of the Kuru-Panchala cultural region around 500 to 400 BCE, mobility and religious interaction.

sources.title: INFLIBNET, Mahajanapadas and the Rise of Magadha
sources.note: University teaching module on Kuru geography, Indraprastha, Koravya tradition, republican classification and lost preeminence.

sources.title: INFLIBNET, Vedic Culture
sources.note: University teaching module on earlier Kuru formation, later Vedic institutions, farming, social order and oral textual context.

sources.title: INFLIBNET, Iron and Urbanization
sources.note: University archaeology module on Painted Grey Ware houses, mixed subsistence, iron technology and gradual urban growth.

sources.title: INFLIBNET, Iron Age Society and Economy
sources.note: University archaeology module on Painted Grey Ware manufacture, tools, settlements and early historic material change.

sources.title: NIOS, The Vedic Age
sources.note: National Institute of Open Schooling survey of later Vedic food, farming, families, hierarchy, work and education limits.

sources.title: NIOS, From Janapadas to Empire
sources.note: National Institute of Open Schooling survey locating Kuru, Indraprastha and the wider sixth-century state system.

sources.title: NIOS, Ancient India Culture and Heritage
sources.note: National Institute of Open Schooling synthesis of food, animals, houses, material culture, crafts and play evidence.

sources.title: NIOS, Evolution of State in India
sources.note: National Institute of Open Schooling account of janapadas, fluid frontiers, monarchies, oligarchies, revenue and armies.

sources.title: INFLIBNET, Approaches to Indian Society and Civilization
sources.note: University anthropology module used cautiously for household, varna, marriage and gender ideals in Vedic textual society.

sources.title: B. B. Lal, Excavation at Hastinapura, Ancient India 10 and 11
sources.note: Archaeological Survey report with stratigraphy, PGW and NBPW material, buildings, tools, food remains, wells, drains and flood evidence.

sources.title: Upinder Singh, A History of Ancient and Early Medieval India
sources.note: Pearson scholarly synthesis of Hastinapura stratigraphy, material evidence and the 600 to 300 BCE urban transition.

sources.title: Garnayak and others, Ironmaking at Hastinapur
sources.note: Current Science study of new excavations, early iron objects, slag analysis, crucibles, coins and the site setting.

sources.title: Jamil Ahmed, Sanitary Management in Northern Black Polished Ware Culture
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeological review distinguishing PGW evidence from later drains, soakage jars, baths, ring wells and sanitation features; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.6907479.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Excavations at Hulas
sources.note: Official excavation report summarizing PGW geography, village houses, rice cultivation, domestic animals and material culture.

sources.title: K. T. M. Hegde, The Painted Grey Ware of India
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeological discussion anchoring PGW as a material category rather than a named ethnic population.

sources.title: Monica L. Smith, Networks of intention in a peripheral landscape
sources.note: Peer-reviewed overview of sixth to fourth-century states, Magadha's rise and later Mauryan incorporation.

sources.title: SuttaCentral, Majjhima Nikaya 10 Pali root text
sources.note: Digital canonical Pali text whose opening places the teaching at Kammassadhamma among the Kurus.

sources.title: SuttaCentral, Majjhima Nikaya 10 English translation
sources.note: Modern scholarly translation used for the Kuru town setting and Buddhist teaching context.

sources.title: UNESCO, Tradition of Vedic chanting
sources.note: Authoritative description of childhood training, tonal accents, recitation patterns and long oral preservation.

sources.title: Vedic Heritage Portal, Paippalada Samhita of the Atharvaveda
sources.note: Government cultural portal discussion of the Kuru-region Parikshit hymn, oral recensions, fever charms and medicinal plants.

sources.title: TITUS, Atharvaveda Saunaka 20.127
sources.note: University-hosted accented Vedic text for the authentic Parikshit household verse and its exact normalized transliteration.

sources.title: Ved Portal, Atharvaveda 20.127.9
sources.note: Accented Devanagari display, word-separated reading and commentary for the selected Kuru household verse.

sources.title: B. V. Subbarayappa, Physicians of ancient India
sources.note: Peer-reviewed history distinguishing Vedic healing rites and plant remedies from the later systematic medical compilations.

sources.title: Coningham and others, Passage to India? Early Use of Brahmi
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeological discussion of the earliest securely dated readable Brahmi evidence and its disputed development.

sources.title: Press Information Bureau, Preservation at Hastinapur
sources.note: Official confirmation that ASI returned to excavate Hastinapur in 2021 to 2023 and displays the findings on site.

proposedOverrides.summary: A late upper-Yamuna janapada with much older Vedic prestige, represented by an atlas polygon whose border and 400 BCE endpoint require explicit caution.

batchIdentityNotes: The exact imported id kuru is indexed circa 500 to 400 BCE and was missing both a card and researched override at the initial audit.
The card treats the target as a late Kuru janapada snapshot, centuries after the main political and ritual prominence reconstructed from later Vedic evidence.
No appliesTo alias is added. The broad vedic-aryans culture layer and separately indexed pancala, surasena, vatsa, kosala, magadha and maurya-empire records remain distinct.
The sole Kuru geometry is one 12-position Polygon with SHA-256 34634e02f599c3b84978d550148cbc1300a3fa1f70738b7094cd667145e4d237.
The imported shape includes tested Hastinapura, Delhi and Ahichchhatra but excludes Kurukshetra and Kaithal, a material identity and border mismatch.
The periods cover only the exact 500 to 400 BCE display window and are explicitly reading lenses rather than invented ruler accessions.
The structured ending is uncertain at the 400 BCE atlas seam. No successor is linked because the next snapshots show a generic layer and then a mixed Magadha boundary before Maurya.
The written-language sample is an earlier Kuru-linked Vedic Sanskrit verse shown in modern Devanagari normalization, with oral-transmission and manuscript-script limits stated.
